title: Judicial Cases Filed Against 32 Citizens Who Attended Khosrow Alikordi’s Funeral
content:
According to HRANA, judicial cases have been filed against 32 citizens in connection with their attendance at the funeral of Khosrow Alikordi, an attorney, in Sabzevar County.

The individuals have been identified as Ahmad Golmishi, Javad Gharehgholi, Saeed Aliabadi, Saman Kheirabadi, Mohammadreza Alikordi, Javad Alikordi, Mohammad Hossein Mohebizadeh, Mojtaba Najafi, Mohammad Sadidi, Reza Tajabadi, Sina Karachi, Mohammadreza Mohammadi, Nasrin Hassani, Esmail Emaminejad, Hossein Pazhoum, Vahideh Haghparast, Hossein Keykhosravi, Mohammad Kargar, Seyed Abolfazl Hosseini, Bahram Rahmani, Ali Manouchehrinia, Yahya Landarani, Ahmad Khaleghi, Seyed Amin Hosseini, Morteza Keyvanlou Shahrestanaki, Seyed Saria Hashemi, Amir Dardeh, Ali Adinehzadeh, Mehdi Farzan, Amirabbas Safa, Mokhtar Golmishi, and Mahmoud Gharehgholi.

According to information received by HRANA, these citizens face charges of “membership in groups, organizations, or branches of organizations established within the country with the aim of disrupting national security.”
snippet: According to HRANA, judicial cases have been filed against 32 citizens in connection with their attendance at the funeral of Khosrow Alikordi, an attorney, in Sabzevar County.

title: Prisoner Executed in Kermanshah Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, a prisoner was executed in Dizelabad Prison in Kermanshah at dawn on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.

The prisoner has been identified as Ershad Abbasi, from Salas-e Babajani County, Kermanshah Province.

According to the report, Mr. Abbasi was arrested approximately two years ago on murder charges and subsequently sentenced to death by a judicial authority. His death sentence was upheld in recent months, and the victim’s family declined to grant forgiveness.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kurdpa, a prisoner was executed in Dizelabad Prison in Kermanshah at dawn on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.

title: Ahmad Tamoui Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison and Fined
content:
According to HRANA, Ahmad Tamoui, a prisoner held in the Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to imprisonment and a fine.

Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, sentenced Tamoui to a total of 15 years in prison and a fine of 1.25 billion tomans on charges of “assembly and collusion against national security” and “carrying and possessing weapons.” Under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, his enforceable sentence has been set at 10 years of discretionary imprisonment, along with the payment of the fine.

Ahmad Tamoui was arrested by IRGC forces in Tehran on February 23, 2026. His arrest reportedly involved violence, and he was subjected to torture following his detention. After being transferred between several security detention facilities, Tamoui was eventually moved to the Greater Tehran Prison.

Ahmad Tamoui has previously been arrested and imprisoned in connection with his activities.
snippet: According to HRANA, Ahmad Tamoui, a prisoner held in the Greater Tehran Prison, has been sentenced to imprisonment and a fine.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January Protests: Ezzatollah Soleimani Sentenced to Seven Years and Eight Months in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, one of the detainees arrested during the January 2026 protests has been sentenced to imprisonment.

Under a verdict issued by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, Soleimani was sentenced to three years and seven months in prison on the charge of “assembly and collusion against national security,” three years and seven months for “insulting religious sanctities,” and six months for “propaganda against the regime.”

Ezzatollah Soleimani was previously arrested by Ministry of Intelligence agents in January 2026. He is currently held at Greater Tehran Prison.

As of the time of this report, no information is available regarding the exact date the verdict was issued, details of the court hearing, or the specific acts underlying the charges against him.

title: One Prisoner Executed at Ardabil Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights, a prisoner was executed at Ardabil Central Prison today, Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The prisoner has been identified as Abasat Alaei, 45, the father of a young daughter.

The report quotes an informed source as saying: “Abasat Alaei was arrested approximately five years ago in connection with a murder case and was subsequently sentenced to death by judicial authorities. On Monday, November 9, he was transferred to solitary confinement in preparation for his execution.”

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.

title: Najmeh Amini Remains on Death Row at Vakilabad Prison as Supreme Court Decision Pending
content:
According to HRANA, Najmeh Amini remains held at Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. Based on information obtained by HRANA, an appeal has been filed against the death sentence issued against Amini. However, the Supreme Court has not yet decided whether to uphold or overturn the verdict.

Najmeh Amini was previously sentenced to death by Criminal Court One of Mashhad on the charge of “insulting the Prophet.” In the initial stages of the proceedings, the charge against her had been described as “insulting the Imams,” but it was subsequently changed during the judicial process.

In a separate case, she was also sentenced by Branch One of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court to a total of 12 years, six months, and one day in prison on charges including “acting against national security” and “propaganda against the regime.”

Amini had previously stated in an audio message from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad that her death sentence was issued on September 16, 2026. In the message, she called on the United Nations, lawyers, human rights activists, and human rights organizations to review her case and demanded that her right to a fair trial be upheld.

title: Two Prisoners Executed at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, the death sentences of two prisoners were carried out at Sepidar Prison in Ahvaz on the morning of Sunday, October 18, 2026.

The prisoners have been identified as Heydarali Kord, 53, and Ali Pirzadeh, 46, both members of the Bakhtiari tribe and residents of Qaleh Tol. Both were married and had children.

According to the report, approximately 14 years ago, the two prisoners were involved in a mass altercation stemming from disputes over agricultural land, during which they committed murder. They were subsequently tried by judicial authorities and sentenced to death on murder charges in a joint case.

As of the time of this report, the executions of these two prisoners have not been announced by domestic media outlets or official sources in Iran.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.

title: Attorney Reza Tayyebnia Sentenced to Six Months in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Reza Tayyebnia has been sentenced to imprisonment.

Based on a verdict issued by Branch 103 of the Criminal Court II of Kohgiluyeh County, Mr. Tayyebnia was sentenced to six months of discretionary imprisonment on the charge of “propaganda against the regime.”

A source close to the lawyer’s family, who confirmed the news to HRANA, stated: “His activities on social media were cited among the grounds for the charges against Reza Tayyebnia.”

The court hearing concerning this charge was held in late September of this year. During the same period, he also presented his defense against the charge of “spreading false information” in another part of his case.

On August 1, 2026, Reza Tayyebnia was summoned to Branch Six of the Prosecutor’s Office of the Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office in Kohgiluyeh County after receiving an official summons.
snippet: According to HRANA, Reza Tayyebnia has been sentenced to imprisonment.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Reports of Violence Against Political Prisoners at Greater Tehran Prison
content:
According to HRANA, information received indicates that officials at Greater Tehran Prison have transferred several prisoners convicted of ordinary crimes to the section housing political prisoners and assigned them responsibilities related to maintaining internal order in the ward.

These individuals, referred to within the prison as “security personnel,” reportedly intervene in certain matters involving the monitoring of other prisoners’ behavior and movements, according to informed sources. However, HRANA has not been able to independently verify the precise scope of authority granted to these individuals or the extent of prison staff supervision over their activities.

The involvement of prisoners in internal prison affairs, including service-related and cultural activities and conveying other inmates’ requests to prison officials, has long been practiced in Iranian prisons. However, existing regulations distinguish between such participation and the delegation of security and disciplinary authority.
snippet: According to HRANA, information received indicates that officials at Greater Tehran Prison have transferred several prisoners convicted of ordinary crimes to the section housing political prisoners

title: Seven Citizens Arrested by Ministry of Intelligence Agents in Bandar Mahshahr
content:
According to HRANA, intelligence agents arrested seven citizens in Bandar Mahshahr.

The identities of the detainees have been confirmed as Adel Othmani, Sultan Othmani, Aziz Gharghouli, Ali Heydari, Mohsen Salihavi, Ali Salihavi, and Tahran Othmani, all residents of the Saadi neighborhood (Hay al-Karama) in Bandar Mahshahr.

Based on information received by HRANA, on Saturday, November 7, 2026, Ministry of Intelligence agents dispatched from Ahvaz raided the homes of these citizens. After searching their residences and confiscating some of their personal belongings, the agents arrested the seven individuals and transferred them to an undisclosed location.

At the time of this report, no information was available regarding the reasons for their arrests, the charges against them, or their whereabouts.
snippet: According to HRANA, intelligence agents arrested seven citizens in Bandar Mahshahr.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Mohammad Mehdi Parsa Sentenced to Death and 20 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Mohammad Mehdi Parsa has been sentenced to death and imprisonment. Based on information received by HRANA, Branch 1 of the Ahvaz Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Ehsan Adibi-Mehr, sentenced Mohammad Mehdi Parsa to death and a total of 20 years in prison. The verdict was issued on November 2, 2026.

According to the verdict, Parsa was sentenced to death on the charge of “moharebeh” (enmity against God) through participation in the destruction of a state-owned bank in Ahvaz. He was also sentenced to 10 years in prison on the charge of participating in illegal gatherings, under provisions prescribing harsher penalties, and an additional 10 years in prison on the charge of collaborating with hostile states.

An informed source close to Parsa told HRANA that he was denied access to a lawyer of his choosing during the judicial proceedings. The source also stated that on the evening of January 8, 2026, during protests in Ahvaz, a state-owned bank was damaged, and following the incident, judicial cases were opened against several protesters.

title: Abolfazl Ghadiani Sentenced to Two Years in Prison in New Case
content:
According to HRANA, political prisoner Abolfazl Ghadiani has been sentenced to prison. Based on information received by HRANA, Ghadiani was sentenced to two years in prison on charges including “propaganda against the regime” and “insulting the Supreme Leader” in a case initiated against him while he was serving his prison sentence.

A source close to the political prisoner’s family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “The verdict was recently issued in absentia by Branch 29 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court and was communicated to him in prison last week. The case was opened against him over a statement he issued that was subsequently made public outside the prison.”

The source further added: “Today, Ghadiani was transferred to a hospital outside the prison for monitoring and treatment of his heart condition. He was subsequently returned to Evin Prison.”

On September 30, 2024, Abolfazl Ghadiani, 81, was arrested by security forces in Tehran to begin serving a three-year-and-six-month prison sentence. He was subsequently transferred to Ward 6 of Evin Prison. The charges brought against him include “insulting the Supreme Leader” and “propaganda against the regime.”

title: Case of Death Row Prisoner Peyman Farah-Avar Referred to Sentence Enforcement Branch
content:
According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Peyman Farah-Avar’s case has been referred to the Sentence Enforcement Branch.

An informed source close to the political prisoner’s family told HRANA: “On Monday, November 9, Mr. Farah-Avar informed his family during a phone call that he had received an official notification indicating that his case had been referred to the Sentence Enforcement Branch.”

Mr. Farah-Avar’s request for retrial, which had been registered with a branch of the Supreme Court, was rejected by the judicial authority on April 26, 2026. His death sentence had previously been upheld by Branch 39 of the Supreme Court in September of 2025.

Mr. Farah-Avar had earlier been sentenced to death on charges of “baghi” (armed rebellion) and “moharebeh” (enmity against God) by Branch 1 of the Rasht Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Ahmad Darvish Goftar.

An informed source close to the political prisoner’s family had previously confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “These charges were brought against Mr. Farah-Avar based on his poetry and protest activities concerning social justice and civil rights.”
snippet: According to HRANA, the news agency of Human Rights Activists in Iran, Peyman Farah-Avar’s case has been referred to the Sentence Enforcement Branch.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Five Individuals Arrested by Security Forces Across Three Provinces
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, the Kermanshah Province Intelligence Department announced that five individuals had been identified and arrested across several provinces in Iran.

In its statement, the Kermanshah Province Intelligence Department claimed that the five individuals were affiliated with separatist groups and had connections with Israeli and U.S. intelligence services. According to the statement, they were identified and arrested in Tehran, Alborz, and Kermanshah provinces.

The statement further alleged that these individuals had also “played a significant role in damaging public property and spreading fear and intimidation in their respective provinces” during the protests of January 2026.

The report provides no further details regarding the detainees’ full identities, their places of detention, the evidence supporting the allegations against them, or the status of the judicial proceedings in their cases.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Mizan News Agency, the Kermanshah Province Intelligence Department announced that five individuals had been identified and arrested across several provinces in Iran.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Zahedan: Three Citizens Killed in Indiscriminate Shooting by Military Forces
content:
According to HRANA, citing the Balochistan Human Rights Documentation Network, three citizens were killed as a result of gunfire by military forces in Zahedan.

Two of the victims have been identified as Omid Jamalzehi, 30, married and a resident of Harmak in Zahedan, and Hanzaleh Jamalzehi, 32,  father of four children, and a resident of Zahedan.

According to the report, the three citizens were traveling from Tehran to Zahedan when, at approximately 3:00 a.m. on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, military forces opened fire on their vehicle in the Lakhshak area, part of Harmak Rural District in Zahedan, without ordering the vehicle to stop or issuing any warning. The occupants of the Peugeot vehicle were struck by gunfire, bringing the vehicle to a halt.

The report further states that, according to eyewitnesses, after the vehicle stopped, military forces fired at Hanzaleh Jamalzehi and another occupant before leaving the scene.

Following calls from local residents to emergency services, the bodies of the three victims were transported by ambulance to the forensic medical facility. Family members and relatives of the victims gathered outside the forensic medical facility in Zahedan.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing the Balochistan Human Rights Documentation Network, three citizens were killed as a result of gunfire by military forces in Zahedan.
